Problem Reported

Client reported intermittent tripping of the standby generator under load during scheduled test runs. Operations staff observed dense black exhaust smoke within the first ten minutes of operation, accompanied by an irregular knocking sound from the engine bay and a noticeable drop in output voltage under partial load. The unit had also failed to reach rated frequency on two prior start attempts, prompting an emergency service call ahead of the facility's planned power-outage window later that week.

Defects Found

Inspection revealed heavily clogged primary and secondary fuel filters restricting flow to the injection pump, along with one partially seized fuel injector on cylinder four. The alternator drive belt was worn and under-tensioned, contributing to voltage instability. Coolant was found below the minimum mark with visible discolouration, and the air filter element showed significant dust loading consistent with the extended interval since last service.

Service Rendered

Engine was isolated and locked out prior to intervention. Both fuel filters were removed and replaced, and the fuel system was bled and primed. The affected injector was removed, ultrasonically cleaned, bench-tested against factory spray-pattern tolerances, and reinstalled with new copper sealing washers. The alternator belt was replaced and tensioned to OEM specification. Coolant system was drained, flushed, and refilled with the correct concentration of long-life coolant, and the air filter element was replaced. The unit was then started, run under a resistive load bank at 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% rated load for 20 minutes each, with all readings logged and verified stable before being returned to automatic standby duty.

Engineer Remarks

Unit is now performing within OEM tolerances across all tested load bands. Recommend reducing the fuel filter replacement interval to 250 hours given the site's fuel storage conditions, and scheduling a full injector service for the remaining cylinders within the next two visits. Coolant levels should be checked monthly by site personnel between scheduled visits to avoid recurrence of low-coolant conditions observed during this call.

Customer Feedback

The BIGDROPS engineer arrived promptly and explained the diagnosis clearly before starting work. The generator now runs noticeably smoother and quieter than before, and the load-bank testing gave us confidence in its readiness for the upcoming outage. We appreciate the practical maintenance advice provided and will follow up on the recommended filter schedule.
